Knowledge Objects

Sources & Documents

Every keyword gets a dedicated object — complete with its own sources, claims, evidence, conflicts, gaps, and AI-visibility report. Click any Knowledge object to open its full, standalone management window.

A knowledge object is created from research or from sources contributing enough claims and evidence to support one — never fabricated because a query volume looked promising. Nothing here caps how many an organization can hold: this screen is built to hold tens, hundreds or thousands of them, searched/filtered/sorted/paginated server-side the same way Sources & Documents is — the browser is never handed the whole collection at once. "Research again" on any row starts a new processing run against whatever sources have been added since — it creates a new version alongside the last one, never overwrites it.

“None found” is a search outcome, not evidence of absence — 4 databases were queried directly, nothing about this species turned up. It is recorded as unknown, not as a negative result.

Close this gap

Three different things you can do — none of them fabricates an answer.

  • Search the literature Queues a research task against clinical trial registries and PubMed. Results land here for review — nothing publishes automatically (§64). Search the literature
  • Add a source PDF, spreadsheet, or a link — if you already hold a trial report or dataset, attach it directly to this gap. Add a source
  • Keep open No action right now. The gap stays visible on the dashboard. Keep open

Other open gaps on this knowledge object

The recommended action follows the gap type — a supplier-certificate gap has no “search the web” button, and a conflict gap is closed by review, not by search or upload.

Execution detail

Attempt chain

    Categories & Master Topic Matrix

    A category carries the section schema its topics should cover. Each cell of the matrix is read from the knowledge base — claims, evidence, conflicts, gaps — never typed in. An empty cell means the section has never been researched for that topic, not that it does not apply.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    New category

    Proposals waiting for a decision

    A section discovered on one topic is proposed to its siblings. Nothing is written into a sibling's knowledge until you decide.

    Coverage audit

    Six dimensions, reported separately and never collapsed into one number: sources, processing, knowledge, evidence, sections and publication. A figure that cannot be known is shown as unknown with the reason — never as zero. If the newest run failed, the last successful audit stays on screen, marked stale.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    History

    Publications & citations

    A publication is built sentence by sentence from claims that already carry their sources, then numbered in Vancouver order by first appearance across the whole document. A sentence with no validated source is marked evidence-unavailable and gets no number — a citation is never invented.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    Website: blog

    Write and publish the articles on your public website, in English and Persian. A post needs an author and a body before it can be published; every edit is kept as a revision with a note, and that history is shown on the published article.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    New post

    Website: page sections

    Show, hide, reorder and retitle the sections of the public home page, separately for each language. The hero carries the page's only main heading and cannot be hidden. The site reads these settings when it is connected to Cloud Core.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    Website: subscribers

    Everyone who joined the newsletter from the public website. An address is stored only with explicit consent, which is recorded with its date and wording. Export as CSV, mark someone unsubscribed, or erase an address completely on request.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    Chat settings

    Controls for the knowledge chat on the public website. Choose which knowledge topics it may read, whether it may ask to research online, which AI resource pays for it, and the limits per person. The chat stays off until you enable it here, and every rule on this screen is enforced on the server — not in the browser.

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    Knowledge topics the chat may read

    Select none to allow every topic in this workspace. Selecting some makes the list exact: the chat can read nothing else, and a question outside it is answered as a knowledge gap rather than guessed.

    Memory Center

    Everything the AI wrote while working: findings, open questions, checkpoints and handoffs — every version kept, with who wrote it and when. PostgreSQL is the canonical store. Reads are live from Cloud Core; exports are produced by the backend.

    Working memory

    Not connected to Cloud Core. Connect on the Dashboard or AI Center screen.

    Every AI resource the system knows about — providers, APIs, models, applications, and research tools. Discovery entries stay "Discovered" until verified from an official source; API and pricing information stays empty until then. This screen reads live from Cloud Core — no sample data.

    Models and their limits

    Limits are what the provider documents for your account. Providers change them, so enter them here rather than trusting a built-in table. Empty means "Unknown" and blocks nothing. A job item larger than a known input limit, or a job reserving more output than a known output limit, fails with CONTEXT_OVERFLOW or OUTPUT_EXCEEDS_MODEL_LIMIT before any call: it is never truncated. Without a max input, the room is the context window minus the output reserve. Requests and tokens per minute are recorded, not yet enforced.

    DashboardAI access

    AI access

    Who may read this site, for what purpose, and on what terms. Every automated client that has ever arrived is listed — including the ones nobody recognises.

    6 agents have no decision yet. They are being allowed through, and the report records that as Not configured rather than as Allowed — because nobody chose it. An unmade decision that quietly behaves like a permission is how a site ends up in a training corpus it never agreed to.

    Rules, most specific first

    The first rule that matches wins and evaluation stops. There is no scoring and no "strictest wins" — you must be able to read this table and predict what happens to a given crawler.

    Access rules in precedence order
    Applies toPurposeDecisionReason given to the agent
    GPTBotAnyForbiddenWe do not permit corpus collection.Edit
    Any AI crawlerTrainingForbiddenTraining use requires a licence.Edit
    Any AI crawlerSearch indexingPaidCommercial licence required — see terms.Edit
    Any AI answering a userAnyFreeNo reason neededEdit

    Read the first two rows together: block training everywhere, but answer a customer's live question freely. That is the whole point of separating purpose from actor. A human visitor is never subject to any of these rules — there is no configuration here that can return 403 to a customer's browser.

    Paid returns HTTP 402 with a link to your terms. It records an intention; nothing in this product meters, invoices or collects anything, and there is deliberately no price field, because a number here would look like a working price.

    A User-Agent header is a claim a request makes about itself. Detected means the header matched a published signature; Probable means a weaker pattern matched; Verified would require reverse-DNS or published-IP confirmation and is not built, so nothing in this product can display it. Blocking by header therefore stops honest agents and does not stop dishonest ones — that is a real limit of this control and is stated here rather than in a footnote.

    Delete “Toranjebin — Scientific Review 2025”?

    This source contributes to 3 knowledge objects, 74 claims and 31 evidence records. Choose how far this goes — the choice is explicit, never a single generic “Delete” (§22).

    • Archive source Stops it being used by anything new. Every claim, evidence record and knowledge contribution it already produced is untouched.
    • Remove from active knowledge The source can no longer be cited by future work. Existing claims and evidence stay published, unchanged.
    • Permanently delete The original file and its derived Markdown, tables and OCR text are removed. 31 evidence records lose their passage-level citation and fall back to source-level only. This cannot be undone.

    An already-archived source (like toranjebin.ir below) skips straight to a choice between staying archived and permanent deletion — there is nothing left to “remove from active”.

    Retire “ترنجبین” (Toranjebin)?

    A knowledge object is the most-connected thing in the system — 248 sources, 1,842 claims and 493 evidence records feed it. What happens here is more limited than for a source.

    • Archive knowledge object Stops it appearing in search and AI visibility. Every source, claim and evidence record it rests on is retained exactly as-is.
    • Permanently delete knowledge content Not available yet. The API only supports archiving a knowledge object today — nothing removes its claims or evidence outright. Shown here disabled rather than as a working-looking button that would not do what it says (§67). Tracked as finding UX-17.

    Open the knowledge gaps this feeds

    Knowledge ObjectsResearch

    Research — regenerate knowledge

    Re-run extraction for an entity after new sources arrive. This never overwrites what exists: it produces a new version beside the current one, so a claim that was approved under the old evidence stays auditable.

    Run again for an entity

    New sources since the last run are picked up automatically. Existing approved claims are carried forward as candidates in the new version — they are not auto-approved, because the evidence behind them may have changed.

      Research question

      Each route is searched separately and never merged: the subject itself, each compound in humans, mechanism, subject and compound together, the compounds in combination, preparations containing the subject, and related species. Only a study of the subject itself can be direct evidence for it.
